title: Model Surgery: Workshop Tuning Cheat Sheet
content:
Context and purpose:
This doc captures notes from the customer-facing ‘Model Surgery’ workshop (Nov 14–15, 2024) for a mid-market SaaS POC where the customer wants sub-150ms p95 generation latency for short chat turns (~40 tokens) while keeping hosted cost near current budget. The goal: concrete model+quant+prompt pipeline recommendations, quick experiments to run, and a short rollout checklist for SEs and infra.

High-level recomendation (TL;DR):
- Primary candidate: 7B open-weights model (v2) compiled to int4 with mixed-kernel fallback to fp16 for attention layers. Expected p95 ~120–160ms on H100/80GB with continuous batching set to 8–12ms tail latency budget.
- Fallback/quality path: 13B quantized to int8 or q4_0 for high-variance prompts; route 5–10% traffic to fp16 13B for golden queries.
- Prompt pipeline: canonicalize user instruction -> short context retrieval (first 3 docs only) -> prefix cache for warm sessions -> token budgeting policy with hard stop at 120 tokens.

Why this combination?
- 7B int4 gives best cost/latency for routine chat where hallucination risk is moderate; int4 quant reduces memory footprint enabling larger batch and lower unit cost.
- 13B fallback keeps semantic correctness for edge cases (long context, multi-step reasoning) without making the whole fleet heavy.
- Mixed-kernel fp16 attention on critical layers preserves quality for numerically sensitive ops where int4 degrades coherency.

Model selection matrix (workshop notes):
- 3B models: Cheapest, sub-100ms on small GPUs but brittle on multi-document reasoning. Not recommended as primary.
- 7B models (v1/v2): Sweet spot for latency/cost. v2 has better instruction tuning; prefer v2 when available.
- 13B models: Significant quality uplift; cost ~2.5–3x vs 7B. Use as fallback or for canary.
- 70B+: Not considered for this POC (cost and infra mismatch).

Quantization strategy and knobs tested (notes from live runs):
- int8 (q8_0): stable quality, moderate memory win, easier to deploy in Dedicated. Latency reduction modest vs fp16.
- int4 (q4_0/q4_1): 35–50% memory reduction, latency wins when kernels are optimized. Watch for numeric instability on long-context synthesis and math.
- Per-channel vs per-tensor: per-channel preferred for critical layers; per-tensor acceptable for feedforward weights to save runtime complexity.
- Kernel selection: prioritize fused attention kernels that support int4; where absent, fall back to fp16 for attention.

Prompt & pipeline tuning checklist (practical items):
- Canonicalization: strip filler punctuation, unify time/date formats, expand shorthand only if user opts-in. Small wins on token count and consistent model behaviour.
- System prompt: keep < 60 tokens; place important instructions at start and repeat only if necessary.
- Context window: only include top-3 retrieved docs unless retrieval confidence > 0.85.
- Caching: enable prefix KV cache for sessions that send multiple short turns. Cache hit reduces cost ~30–45% in our traces.
- Prompt templates: supply 2 variations (concise and verbose). Evaluate both with A/B for quality/cost tradeoffs.
- Temperature schedule: default 0.0–0.2 for deterministic responses; allow 0.6+ for exploratory feature in beta.

Experiment matrix to run (quick wins prioritized):
1) 7B fp16 vs 7B int4 (q4_0) — measure p95, p50, token cost per 1k requests, and task accuracy on 200-shot eval set. (Metric: p95 target < 150ms).
2) 7B int4 + attention fallback to fp16 on offending prompts — observe % of fallbacks and quality delta.
3) Route 10% to 13B fp16 for long-context prompts > 150 tokens; measure false-positive routing rate.
4) Vary batching window: 5ms/10ms/20ms to find knee for latency SLO vs tokens/sec.
5) Evaluate prefix caching impact on multi-turn sessions: cold vs warm session cost delta.

Infrastructure mapping and expected perf (empirical notes):
- H100 80GB (single-GPU): 7B int4 p95 ~110–140ms for single-turn 40 tokens with continuous batching tuned to 8ms.
- A100 40GB: 7B int4 p95 ~150–190ms; ok for non-strict SLOs.
- Multi-GPU sharding: avoid for 7B; increases latency due to cross-GPU comms. Use multi-GPU for 13B+.

Routing and rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (Lab): run experiments on dedicated staging cluster (H100 nodes). Validate int4 kernels and fallback paths.
- Phase 1 (Canary): 5% traffic on hosted API -> 7B int4 primary, 13B fallback (10% of 5% routed). Monitor hallucination and latency.
- Phase 2 (Gradual): 25% -> 50% if p95 < 160ms and quality regression < 3% on eval set.
- Phase 3 (GA): full rollout with alerting and automatic rollback to fp16 7B if quality alerts triggered.

Monitoring and eval signals to track: (minimum set)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per model and per route
- Cost: tokens per request and billed tokens per minute
- Quality: task-specific exact match and BLEU-ish metrics for retrieval QA; also prompt-level human review sample (1% of requests)
- Fallback rate: % requests that triggered attention fp16 fallback or reroute to 13B
- Divergence alerts: model output drift vs baseline (embedding distance + behavior tests)

Common failure modes observed in workshop:
- Numeric drift on tables/math when using aggressive int4 quant -> mitigate by keeping final linear layers in fp16 or using per-channel quantization there.
- Prompt sensitivity after quantization: small prefix wording changes caused hallucinations for certain prompts. Mitigation: increase canary traffic to find fragility and add guardrail prompts (explicit step-by-step constraints).
- Unexpected cold-cache latency spikes: add warm-up traces after autoscale events and tune eviction policy to keep recent sessions.

Sample prompt templates (recommended):
- Concise assistant: "System: You are a concise assistant. Use at most 80 tokens. User: {user_input}"
- Retrieval-augmented: "System: Use the following documents to answer. If not in docs, say 'I don’t know'. Docs: {top_docs}
User: {user_input}"

Action items for SEs (next 2 weeks):
- Aisha: spin up staging nodes, deploy 7B int4 build, and run exp (1). (JIRA: SE-1420)
- Ben: implement prefix-caching prototype in the pipeline; add metrics export for cache hit/miss.
- Luis: prepare eval harness (200-shot) with customer-specific prompts and scoring rules.
- Mei: write canary monitoring dashboard and configure alerts (latency, fallback rate, quality regression).

Rollout guardrails (must-haves before canary):
- Automated canary rollback (traffic cut) on quality regression >5% or p95 > 200ms for >10 minutes.
- Sampling for human review at 1% traffic.
- Privacy check: ensure retrieval snippets are redaction-reviewed for PII before included in context.

Appendix - quick cheat entries:
- If hallucinations spike with int4: enable per-channel quant for last MLP and attention proj layers, run a 100-sample sanity test.
- If p95 latency is high despite batching: reduce max batch size and shorten batching window; prioritize tail latency over throughput for interactive SLOs.
- Short-term cost tuning: increase batch size during off-peak hours and set a lower cost-route for non-critical background tasks.

Notes / unresolved questions from workshop:
- Need repository of golden prompts from customer to calibrate fallback heuristics (action: Luis).
- Confirm preferred hardware for Dedicated contract (H100 availability vs A100 pricing tradeoff).

End of doc.
